questions.question: In bad weather, you should:

options.text: Steer off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, do not slam on the brakes or make sharp turns. These actions make it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: Give the right-of-way to any pedestrian who is:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing any street.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing the street anywhere. This includes marked and unmarked crosswalks. Always let pedestrians cross safely.

questions.question: You should allow extra space when following:

options.text: A station wagon.
A driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.
A small passenger car.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of large vehicles like trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles with trailers may not see you behind them. Stay far back. Large vehicles also block your view of the road ahead.

questions.question: You want to park uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way do you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels away from the center. If your brakes fail, the car will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Leave the front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb. When parking uphill without a curb or parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb or edge.

questions.question: When stopping on snow or ice with Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
Stay off the brakes and let the car stop on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly and keep holding it. The ABS will pump the brakes for you faster than you can.

questions.question: If your car's rear end skids to the left, you should:

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap the brakes and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, steer in the direction you want the front to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This straightens out your vehicle.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Right, not a privilege.
Privilege, not a right.
Requirement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege, not a right.
questions.explanation: A driver license is a privilege. You must earn it and keep it by following the law.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left from a two-way street, you should drive:

options.text: Near the right-hand side of the road.
Near the centerline.
On the left of the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the centerline.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street, stay near the centerline. Turn just before your car reaches the center of the intersection. Turn into the first legal lane available.

questions.question: When should you yield your right-of-way?

options.text: Often, even at controlled intersections.
Whenever it helps prevent collisions.
Never. It confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it helps prevent collisions.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Yield whenever it helps prevent a crash.

questions.question: When passing, when should you move back into the right lane?

options.text: When you are one car length ahead of the car you passed.
When you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You need enough space to return to your lane safely. When you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror, you have enough room and it is safe to return to the right lane.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an upcoming corner. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Other cars also turning left.
All cars coming toward you.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: All cars coming toward you.
questions.explanation: When you turn left, you must let all oncoming cars pass first. This includes pedestrians, bicycles, and other vehicles with a green light.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Apply your brakes.
Let go of the steering wheel.
Press your head firmly against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If your car is hit from behind, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel. Press yourself against your seat and push your head against the headrest to prevent whiplash. Be ready to brake to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for traffic merging from the right.
Merge to the right.
Turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for traffic merging from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to dangers ahead. This sign warns you that cars may merge into your lane from the right.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Unfasten your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Unfasten your seat belt.
questions.explanation: If your car is hit from behind, keep your seat belt fastened. Brace yourself by pressing against your seat and pushing your head against the headrest to prevent whiplash. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and be ready to brake.

questions.question: If you come to an intersection and you cannot see clearly to the side, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly.
questions.explanation: Slow down when approaching an intersection. If you cannot see clearly, stop completely. Then move forward slowly until you can see all directions clearly before proceeding.

questions.question: On a road with a single broken white centerline, what can you do?

options.text: You must stay in your lane.
You may cross the centerline to change lanes.
You may change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the centerline to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines mean both lanes go the same direction. A broken white line means you can pass other vehicles when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car in front of you.
Keep your eyes moving to spot hazards ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving to spot hazards ahead.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means always looking ahead for dangers. Staring straight ahead at the road is dangerous. Scan the road and stay alert to cars around you.

questions.question: A police officer tells you to go through a red light. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through the intersection.
Stop completely before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A police officer directing traffic overrides all traffic signals and signs. Always follow the officer's directions.

questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, what must you do?

options.text: Give the right-of-way to traffic that could cause a crash.
Give the right-of-way only to cars on your right.
Always slow down and go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to traffic that could cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Give the right-of-way to any crossing or merging traffic that is close enough to create a danger.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
Turn on your high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead better.
Keep the instrument panel lights bright so other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night than during the day. You cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop your vehicle within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: There are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked vehicles to your right. Which way should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
Down the middle, between the oncoming and parked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Down the middle, between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
questions.explanation: When oncoming vehicles are to your left and parked vehicles are to your right, steer down the middle. This keeps you away from both dangers.

questions.question: If dust or smoke is blowing across the road and you cannot see other vehicles, what should you turn on?

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles. This helps other drivers see you too.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to watch for animals, people, and bicycles that may cross the road.

questions.question: Which statement about roadwork zones is true?

options.text: Traffic fines are the same in work zones as in normal conditions.
You must slow down in the work zone.
Slow down only if you see workers present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down in the work zone.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop in work zones. Careful driving in work zones keeps drivers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and workers safe.
